research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical releases and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Football statistics coverage
verified_claims: The release covers the 2025 to 2026 domestic season and regulated matches played in and outside England and Wales.
limitations: Summer 2026 international-tournament data and revisions are not included yet.

sources.name: Football arrest and police-action scope
verified_claims: The arrest series includes arrests and other police actions connected with regulated matches and specified other offences.
limitations: The combined series is not a count of arrests alone in every season.

sources.name: Football banning-order definition
verified_claims: A football banning order is a court-imposed order intended to prevent violence or disorder connected with regulated football matches.
limitations: An order in force is not evidence of a current incident at a specific place.

sources.name: Reported football incident source
verified_claims: Reported incidents are submitted to UKFPU by dedicated football officers and may include information from bodies such as the FA and Kick It Out.
limitations: Reported incidents are administrative reports and may not represent unique people or criminal offences.

sources.name: Online hate and abuse threshold
verified_claims: Online hate and abuse figures cover reports to relevant bodies that met specified criteria and threshold tests.
limitations: Reports below the threshold or made elsewhere are outside the published count.

sources.name: Domestic football season period
verified_claims: The domestic season covered June 2025 to May 2026.
limitations: Season-based figures must not be compared with unmatched calendar-year periods.

sources.name: Unauthorised-entry offence addition
verified_claims: Unauthorised entry was added to Schedule 1 on 22 March 2026 and appears for the first time in this release.
limitations: The new offence creates a classification break within the season.

sources.name: Banning order after unauthorised entry
verified_claims: A football banning order can be made following conviction for unauthorised entry.
limitations: The availability of an order does not mean every conviction produced one.

sources.name: New safeguarding incident categories
verified_claims: Sexism and misogyny and violence against women and girls were included as reported-incident categories for the first time.
limitations: The added categories can raise reported totals without a like-for-like increase.

sources.name: Football arrests and actions total
verified_claims: There were 1,963 football-related arrests and other police actions for regulated matches in England and Wales.
limitations: The total combines arrests with other police actions.

sources.name: Football arrests annual comparison
verified_claims: The 1,963 total was 2% lower than the equivalent 2024 to 2025 matches.
limitations: Comparisons must use equivalent periods and definitions.

sources.name: Unauthorised-entry actions
verified_claims: Forty-five arrests and other police actions were recorded for unauthorised entry.
limitations: The offence was available only from 22 March 2026.

sources.name: Football banning orders in force
verified_claims: There were 2,460 football banning orders in force on 1 June 2026.
limitations: The stock includes orders issued in earlier seasons.

sources.name: New football banning orders
verified_claims: Seven hundred and one new banning orders were issued during the domestic season.
limitations: New orders are court outcomes and not incident counts.

sources.name: Matches with reported incidents
verified_claims: Incidents were reported in relation to 1,644 matches, 4% more than the previous domestic season.
limitations: The increase was largely affected by new incident categories.

sources.name: Inside-stadium share
verified_claims: Just over half of arrests and other police actions occurred inside football stadia.
limitations: The remaining events may occur elsewhere and cannot be assigned to a stadium parcel.

sources.name: Attendance-normalised rate
verified_claims: The release calculated 4.0 arrests and other police actions per 100,000 attendees for covered men's competitions.
limitations: The rate excludes some competitions and relies on external attendance sources.

sources.name: British Transport Police actions
verified_claims: British Transport Police reported 99 football-related arrests and other police actions under Schedule 1.
limitations: BTP figures relate to transport policing and should not be assigned to match venues.

sources.name: Other-arrest offence detail limitation
verified_claims: The recording method for 'other' arrests does not support publication by offence type.
limitations: The offence type must not be inferred from the aggregate category.

sources.name: Football collection-period break
verified_claims: The 2024 to 2025 collection covered ten months, while 2025 to 2026 covered twelve months, so comparisons use the equivalent ten-month period.
limitations: Full-season totals from the two years are not directly like-for-like.
